title: His face shone (Luke 9:28–36)
hookLine: he was praying when his face changed; Moses and Elijah talk of his departure

lines: EIGHT DAYS LATER, UP A MOUNTAIN.
cards: About eight days after the talk of the cross, Jesus takes three friends, Peter, John and James, and climbs a mountain. Luke tells us why: they went up "to pray."
Some people describe a place, a hospital chapel, a hilltop, a kitchen at 4am, where they sat in prayer or silence long enough that something in the room seemed to shift.
The three disciples are tired; Luke says they were "heavy with sleep." And while they fight to keep their eyes open, Jesus keeps praying. Then his face begins to change.

teach.h: AS HE PRAYED, HIS FACE CHANGED.
teach.b: In the King James words: "And as he prayed, the fashion of his countenance was altered, and his raiment was white and glistering." As he prayed: that's Luke's own emphasis.
Matthew says his face did shine as the sun; Luke says it changed while he was praying. The light comes in the middle of prayer.
Then two men are talking with him, Moses and Elijah, the lawgiver and the prophet. In Exodus, Moses' own face shone after he spoke with God on a mountain. And what are they talking about?

They "spake of his decease which he should accomplish at Jerusalem." Decease, in Greek, is exodos: a departure, a way out. Some readers hear in it the book of Exodus, Moses leading Israel out of slavery.

Here, beside Moses, Jesus talks about his own exodus, the death and rising waiting for him in Jerusalem. Peter wakes enough to say something: "Master, it is good for us to be here: and let us make three tabernacles."
Three shelters. Stay, make it last. Luke adds kindly that he didn't know what he was saying.
Then a cloud covers them, and a voice: "This is my beloved Son: hear him."

teach.h: AS HE PRAYED, THE FASHION OF HIS COUNTENANCE WAS ALTERED.
teach.b: When the cloud lifts, Jesus is alone, and they tell no one in those days. Churches remember this as the Transfiguration, the change of form. But in Luke, the change doesn't come from nowhere.

how: Churches in several traditions keep a feast of the Transfiguration, and some Protestant churches mark Transfiguration Sunday just before Lent.

o: a departure, a way out, a going out
a mountain where God speaks to prophets
a bright cloud that hides God's glory

games.q: what's inside Luke 9:28–36 — tap the pairs.
p: this is my beloved Son: hear him

s: the three disciples stayed wide awake on the mountain
Luke says they were heavy with sleep.
Luke says Moses and Elijah talked about his exodus
his decease, exodos, to be accomplished at Jerusalem.
Peter suggested building one shelter for Jesus
he suggested three: for Jesus, Moses and Elijah.

games.q: you're Peter, half asleep, and you see Jesus shining, with Moses and Elijah. what do you say?
o: it's good to be here; let's build three shelters.
games.why: Peter wants to build three tabernacles and make it last. Luke adds that he didn't know what he was saying.

practice: Don't aim for a vision; aim for staying, past the point where you'd normally stop, through the noisy first minute of lists and worries and tiredness.

Notice if something softens, a thought loosening, your shoulders dropping, and don't grab at it, the way Peter wanted to build shelters. If you pray, you can let the words run out and simply stay; if you don't, simply stay.

wordCard.voice: Exodos, Greek for a going out, a departure: on a mountain, while Jesus prays, his face changes, and Moses and Elijah speak with him about his coming death and rising at Jerusalem.

orig.note: Greek: a going out, departure. the "decease" of Luke 9:31, and the name of the book of Exodus.
